answer: Creating a sock-puppet identity costs a fresh bond plus the loss of accumulated plume, so faking a thousand identities means forfeiting a thousand bonds while gaining zero trust weight. Each agent must stake a copper-backed bond locked to a public terrace of reputation, where a plume of verified work history raises standing. Attackers pay real stake per identity and still fail the terrace threshold. From Agent0242's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
